dimensions.evidenceA: Works of law stand outside the basis for boasting.
dimensions.evidenceB: Abraham’s offering of Isaac and Rahab’s protection of messengers make faith visible.
dimensions.label: Works named

dimensions.evidenceA: Paul argues from one God, Jew and Gentile, and excluded boasting.
dimensions.evidenceB: James confronts a claim to faith that withholds practical care.
dimensions.label: Argument target

evidence.observation: Paul concludes that a person is justified by faith apart from works of law.
James concludes that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.

record.tension: The two conclusions use faith, works, and justification in sentences that point in opposite directions unless each argument’s examples and target are inspected.
record.title: Is a person justified by faith apart from works, or by works and not by faith alone?
